ProgressBar

Determinate progress track exposed as role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max.

Live example

The example needs JavaScript; the usage below shows the markup.

Usage

Determinate progress track for multi-step enrollment forms, file uploads, or profile completion.

<ProgressBar value={60} label="Etapa 3 de 5" />
<ProgressBar value={100} tone="success" />

Pill-shaped to match the brand's rounded system. Pair with label for multi-step flows so users know where they stand.

The track is a role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max. It takes its accessible name from label; when the bar has no visible label, pass ariaLabel instead ("Envio de documentos").

Plain HTML contract

<div class="rse-progress-bar rse-progress-bar--success" style="--rse-progress-bar-value:60%">
  <div class="rse-progress-bar__label"><span>Etapa 3 de 5</span><span>60%</span></div>
  <div class="rse-progress-bar__track" role="progressbar" aria-valuenow="60" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-label="Etapa 3 de 5">
    <div class="rse-progress-bar__fill"></div>
  </div>
</div>

Keep the custom property, visible percentage and ARIA value in sync, within 0–100. Tone modifiers are --primary (default), --success, and --danger. React forwards the ref and native div attributes to the outer div; ariaLabel names the inner progressbar. className and caller style are merged at the root. Width is the only generated inline custom property.

Props

PropTypeRequiredNotes
valuenumber—0-100
toneprimary success danger—
labelstring—Optional caption shown above the track, with the % on the right
ariaLabelstring—Accessible name when there is no visible label (default "Progresso")

Also accepts every attribute of React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, a ref and className.

CSS classes

Blocks
.rse-progress-bar
Elements
.rse-progress-bar__fill .rse-progress-bar__label .rse-progress-bar__track
Modifiers
.rse-progress-bar--danger (tone) .rse-progress-bar--success (tone)
